_method: eBay does not serve its sold listings to a script (HTTP 403 without a session), so every price here is a tracker's aggregation of completed eBay sales, not listings counted one by one: getpcparts.com for the older cards, pcpartvalue.com (medians of completed sales) for the GeForce 40 series, cross-checked against jawa.gg, a used marketplace that publishes its own completed sales, and against active asking prices. Each figure blends the models of a card, reference and premium. The used market was rising fast when this was collected, 5 to 8 percent over 30 days for the older cards and 10 to 27 percent over 90 days for the 40 series, so read the table as a snapshot of September 2026. The GeForce 50 series is a special case: only active asking prices were available for it, in the middle of a memory shortage that has every 50 series card 30 to 130 percent above its launch price, so those rows carry low confidence. Where the used asking price stands above new retail, as it does for the RTX 5090, the table takes the retail price, because that is what the card really costs to get.

RTX 2070 Super.note: the asking prices average $228, a gap of 24 percent against the sold figure, far wider than the 4 to 11 percent of the other cards: the clearing price is probably $175 to $200

RTX 3050.note: dearer than the faster RTX 2060 and near the RTX 2070: it is still sold new (about $259), which anchors the used price to retail rather than to performance

RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB.note: the sources disagree by a third ($411 jawa.gg, $547 pcpartvalue, $650 asking); the 16 GB card goes for about 65 percent more than the 8 GB one ($330), bought for the memory rather than for games

RTX 4070 Ti Super.note: three sales only, and the sources span $735 to $1020: read it as $800 to $900

RTX 4080.note: the one solid figure of the 40 series: jawa.gg independently gives $892 over 34 sales

RTX 4090.note: about 1.75 times its launch price of $1599, which four trackers agree on: the memory of the AI market

RTX 3060.note: pcprice.watch gives EUR 249 over 1447 completed sales, which agrees

RTX 3070.note: the best sampled card of the set, and pcprice.watch agrees over 1222 sales

RTX 3080 10 GB.note: three trackers land within a few percent: $357.59, $358 and EUR 354

RTX 3080 Ti.note: the other tracker had two sales only, so this one is the headline

RTX 3090.note: the trackers disagree badly for the same month ($1032 to $1499) and one 90 day average sits 40 percent under its own 30 day average; the 24 GB cards trade on the demand for memory, not on their speed

RTX 3090 Ti.note: at or above its launch price, like the RTX 3090

RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB.note: the pool of listings mixes the 8 GB and 16 GB cards, so the figure is biased low for the 16 GB one

RTX 5080.note: completed sales across seven markets give about $1490, which agrees

RTX 5090.note: the used asking price ($5099) is ABOVE new retail ($4600), a scalper premium on a card that is hard to buy: the table takes the retail price

A100 SXM4 40 GB.note: no completed sale could be verified; the band comes from a buying guide that names no source, and the SXM4 40 GB barely trades (the 80 GB card is the volume part). It also needs an SXM carrier board, so it is not a card one simply buys and plugs in

H200.note: it does trade, but only asking prices are published, from $40k to $78k: no median is honest here
